external_entities.name: customer
external_entities.description: A person who browses and places orders through the mobile app and receives fax confirmations.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app
external_entities.notes: The source does not describe the customer's trust zone or authentication context.

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: Sokify's mobile application through which customers browse and order.
processes.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app
processes.notes: The source does not state how the app authenticates to the API.

processes.name: web API
processes.description: The API used by the mobile app to handle customer and order data, update catalogue information, and hand orders to SIMS.
processes.source_excerpt: The app talks to the web API over HTTP — not HTTPS
processes.notes: Authentication is explicitly unidentified: "Nobody here can tell me what the API does about authentication".

processes.name: stock and inventory system
processes.description: The stock and inventory system, referred to as SIMS, that receives orders and handles delivery-address and dispatch processing.
processes.source_excerpt: SIMS, our stock and inventory system
processes.notes: The source says SIMS has been running since long before the app existed.

processes.name: fax gateway
processes.description: A gateway that receives dispatch notes and faxes customer confirmations using the number stored against the order.
processes.source_excerpt: it sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway, which faxes the customer
processes.notes: The source says nobody checks whether the fax arrived at the right place.

processes.name: macros
processes.description: Spreadsheet macros that send SQL statements directly to the web API to change prices and product copy.
processes.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API
processes.notes: The macros are described as a stopgap that is still in use.

data_stores.name: user database
data_stores.description: The database where the web API keeps customer names, addresses, and the card they paid with.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database: name, address, and the card they paid with.
data_stores.notes: The source says nobody can tell whether the user database is encrypted.

data_stores.name: flat file
data_stores.description: A flat file kept alongside SIMS containing delivery addresses only.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes the delivery address into a flat file kept alongside it — only addresses go in that file, nothing else
data_stores.notes: The source says nobody can tell whether the flat file is encrypted.

data_stores.name: spreadsheet
data_stores.description: The marketing catalogue containing prices and product copy, with macros that send SQL statements to the web API.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Marketing keep the catalogue in a spreadsheet.
data_stores.notes: The spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.

data_flows.name: browse and order
data_flows.description: Customer browsing and ordering activity sent to the mobile app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app
data_flows.notes: The source does not specify the protocol or authentication.

data_flows.name: submit orders
data_flows.description: The mobile app communicates customer browsing and order activity to the web API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app talks to the web API over HTTP — not HTTPS
data_flows.notes: The source explicitly states HTTP rather than HTTPS. Authentication is unknown: "Nobody here can tell me what the API does about authentication".

data_flows.name: store customer data
data_flows.description: The web API stores customer names, addresses, and payment-card information in the user database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database: name, address, and the card they paid with.
data_flows.notes: The source does not state authentication for this interaction.
data_flows.data_description: Customer name, address, and the card they paid with

data_flows.name: hand over order
data_flows.description: The web API hands an order to SIMS.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When an order is placed the API hands the order over to SIMS

data_flows.name: write address
data_flows.description: SIMS writes the delivery address into the flat file.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes the delivery address into a flat file kept alongside it

data_flows.name: send dispatch note
data_flows.description: SIMS sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway.
data_flows.source_excerpt: it sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway

data_flows.name: fax confirmation
data_flows.description: The fax gateway faxes a confirmation containing the customer's name and address to the customer.
data_flows.source_excerpt: which faxes the customer a confirmation with their name and address on it
data_flows.notes: The gateway dials the number stored against the order, and nobody checks that the fax arrived at the right place.

data_flows.name: change catalogue
data_flows.description: Spreadsheet macros send SQL statements to the web API to change prices and product copy.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API to change prices and product copy
data_flows.notes: The source does not state authentication or encryption for this interaction.

trust_boundaries.name: office
trust_boundaries.description: The office location where the marketing laptop hosting the spreadsheet is located.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.

assumptions.assumption: The web API is internet-facing because customers use the online mobile app to communicate with it.
assumptions.basis: The source says Sokify sells socks online, customers use the mobile app, and the app talks to the web API.

assumptions.assumption: The user database has confidential data because it contains customer names, addresses, and payment-card information.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the user database contains customer name, address, and the card they paid with.

assumptions.assumption: The flat file has confidential data because it contains customer delivery addresses.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the flat file contains delivery addresses.
